subject: [Post-call] Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - ZenHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Klein <jared.klein@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@zenhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Jared / Priya -

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points / goals (as I heard them):
- Predictable throughput for clinical ingestion pipelines: ~600 concurrent sessions at peak (medical transcription + summarization).
- Data isolation / compliance: patient PHI must remain in a dedicated, customer-controlled VPC with strict egress rules.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation < 350ms for short prompts (<= 512 tokens), targeted 99th < 800ms for longer jobs.
- Cost predictability: committed monthly capacity vs variable burst behavior; want clear unit economics to present to finance.

Suggested dedicated capacity profile (ballpark):
- Reserved: 8x A10G-equivalent GPUs (can discuss instance families) with private subnets and KMS-managed keys.
- Autoscale policy: baseline 6 GPUs, scale to 12 for sustained bursts up to 48h, burst credits for seasonal peaks.
- Isolation: no noisy-tenant sharing; dedicated KV-cache and storage; audit log forwarding to your Splunk instance.

Operational / SLA targets discussed:
- Uptime SLA: 99.9% for the dedicated pool
- Latency SLOs as above; fallback policy to a slightly cheaper model variant for non-critical traffic
- Retention & logging: 90-day logs by default, option to extend to 1 year for audit requests

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) Exact token distribution and average prompt/response length (Jared to share a sampled distribution).
2) Confirmation on inbound/outbound network restrictions for the VPC; Priya to share the SecOps policy doc.
3) Any hard constraints on model choice (open vs licensed models) for accuracy/regulatory reasons.

Attachments: attached a short draft proposal with the suggested capacity and a draft SOW for legal review.

Next steps / owners:
- Jared: share sample token distribution & volume forecast by EOD Mon (3/16).
- Priya: share SecOps network requirements and any encryption policy by next Wed (3/18).
- Vivek: I'll loop you on the infra details; please propose a sizing validation test (10k reqs/day) and an in-region pilot plan.
- Marissa (me): I will send a formal proposal + calendar invites for a technical sizing call next week.

Proposed meeting: Tech sizing (1hr) - Tue 3/17 10:00am PT - I'll send calendar invite once you confirm.

Appreciate the time - excited to help ZenHealth get a predictable, compliant inference stack in prod.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - great write-up and yes, that matches our notes. A few clarifications: 

- Token distribution: we'll extract a day-of-week sample and send to you by Mon (3/16). Average prompt ~120 tokens, average generation ~280 tokens, peak sequences hit ~1.2k tokens for longer summarization jobs but those are <5% of traffic.
- For the model choice, clinical accuracy matters - we need to use models validated on clinical data or our own fine-tune. We'll list constraints in the SecOps doc.
- On burst behavior: can you confirm whether burst-to-12 GPUs would be billed at the committed rate or at an overage rate? We want to model cost in the finance deck.

Happy to join the sizing call on Tue 3/17. Please include an agenda for the hour (infra + test plan + timeline).

Jared

Hey team - quick technical notes from my side after listening in: 

- GPU sizing: 8x A10G-equivalent is a sensible starting point for the mix you described, but we'll validate with a 48-hour soak test on 6 GPUs to confirm p95 latency and token throughput. If your peak jobs (1.2k tokens) are frequent, we should consider slightly more memory-optimized instances.
- KV cache: we'll provision customer-dedicated KV nodes to avoid cross-tenant contamination; the cache TTLs can be tuned per route.
- Networking: to meet your egress restrictions, we can deploy a private control plane with floating NAT disabled; logs can be forwarded to your Splunk via a secure collector.

I'll put together a short sizing test plan and share by EOD. For the billing question Jared raised: typically bursts above committed capacity use pre-negotiated overage rates; I'll have revisions for committed vs burst pricing in the proposal PDF so finance can model it.

-Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
